name: Steroid back acne management

lead: Steroid back acne is acne on the back and shoulders that people attribute to anabolic steroid or testosterone use. People who train for physique want to keep that area clear so the back and shoulders look clean as well as built.

Androgen levels rise, sebum output increases, and breakouts appear on the oil-rich skin of the back. Wikipedia describes acne as a recognised effect of anabolic-androgenic steroids and testosterone replacement. Available reference material covers general acne and androgens; no trial dedicated to back acne from performance-enhancing steroids was found.

paras: People generally lean on standard acne care for the back: regular washing after training, clean fabrics against the skin, and over-the-counter or prescribed acne products. Forum discussion treats it as an ongoing side effect to manage rather than a one-time fix, and persistent cases are usually taken to a clinician.
Anabolic steroids carry broader legal and health risks beyond skin. Severe or scarring acne is usually managed by clinicians, and prescription acne drugs have their own side effects.

angle.text: The goal is a clear back and shoulders while building a physique. Rising androgen levels increase sebum output, and back and shoulder acne appears; acne is a recognised effect of anabolic steroids and testosterone. Management advice draws mostly on general acne information.

lead: Steroid back acne (often called bacne in forums) refers to acne on the back and shoulders that people attribute to anabolic-androgenic steroid or testosterone use. Wikipedia states that anabolic-androgenic steroids and testosterone replacement can cause acne, and describes it as steroid acne [1].
The available reference material is limited to general acne information, and no published trial dedicated to back acne from performance-enhancing steroids was identified.

paras: Androgens such as testosterone and DHT are linked to acne because they increase sebum production, and acne does not develop in people with complete androgen insensitivity syndrome [1]. Conventional acne treatments listed by Wikipedia include topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, antibiotics and, for severe acne, isotretinoin [1].
